pr.title: Stream replay: snapshots, filters, and the caught-up boundary
pr.body:
Fixes #81

`GET /api/v1/stream` grows from the handshake into historical replay: subscribe-time snapshots from the live owners, an enumerated filter grammar, a composite cursor at rest, filtered replay to a fixed high-water mark, `score.stream.caught_up`, and a clean close — `follow=true` hits the tested `FOLLOW_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` seam for #82.

## What's here

- **`apps/web/src/telemetry/stream/`** (new sub-feature, own front door):
  - `query.policy.ts` — the filter grammar (`projects`, `signals`, `names`, `phases`, `outcomes`, `trace_id`, `subject_kind`+`subject_id`, `since`/`until`, `follow`): exact-match and time-window only; unknown param → 400 `FILTER_UNKNOWN`, bad value → 400 `FILTER_INVALID`. `since`/`until` reuse core's `isRfc3339`, so calendar-invalid dates are rejected, not normalized.
  - `cursor.render.ts` — the `Last-Event-ID` composite cursor: base64url JSON of every selected project/source's `{segment, byte_offset}`; garbage decodes to 400 `CURSOR_UNPARSEABLE`.
  - `snapshot.service.ts` + `snapshot.render.ts` — one owner read per subscribe (config keys, resolved.json, status.json, supervisor jobs), health via #76's `healthFor`, allowlisted payloads only (no paths, no free error/gate text). Unreadable config or supervisor table rides every snapshot as an explicit warning instead of posing as a complete fleet.
  - `replay.policy.ts` + `replay.service.ts` — marks captured once at subscribe (each file's byte length), ≤500-record I/O cycles to the mark, torn tails withheld, per-segment `RECORD_UNPARSEABLE`/`SEGMENT_UNREADABLE` warnings so a shortfall against the mark is never silent. A cursor component naming a deleted segment → `410 Gone` before any event. The replay generator returns the final composite cursor so `caught_up` rests at the true position even when trailing records were filtered out.
  - `stream.service.ts` — orchestration; one read-time stamp for the whole subscribe.
- **Route** — thin HTTP layer: parses URL + `Last-Event-ID`, streams the frame generator; explicit `POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE → 405`. Errors render as the #80 envelope with enum-only reasons.
- **Tests** — golden transcripts (fleet + project snapshots with reasons/freshness, trace replay reconstructing one issue across phases, log-record replay, caught_up, both follow closes), continuous-write termination at the fixed mark, batch-cap proof at the cycle level, cursor resume/resync/410 matrix, filter grammar + matching tables, route HTTP shaping.

## Outside the stated scope, with reasons

- `packages/core/src/observation/jobs.service.ts` (new) — the daemon test suite's no-lifecycle-route guard bars `apps/web` from importing `@score/core/supervisor` at all, while the issue requires snapshots from `SupervisorAdapter.status()`. This read-only seam (status alone, runner injected by the app) satisfies both; membership degrades to `null` = unknown, surfaced as `SUPERVISOR_UNREADABLE`, never an empty-but-complete job table.
- `packages/core/src/telemetry/telemetry.policy.ts` — exported the existing `isRfc3339` (no behavior change) so the grammar holds record timestamps' bar.
- `packages/shared/src/adapters/command-runner.service.ts` — a one-line `env` cast: the web TS program now includes this file transitively and Next's `ProcessEnv` augmentation rejects a plain string record. Runtime unchanged.

## Review notes

Codex review ran over the diff; fixed: stale `caught_up` cursor under trailing filtered records, calendar-invalid timestamps, silent supervisor-failure→DISABLED health, pull-time snapshot stamps, core composing a runner, unprovable batch cap, `.service` modules without classes. Declined one finding — treating an offset-zero cursor naming a segment with no retained evidence around it as consumed rather than 410: that case is indistinguishable from a date that never had records (e.g. a cursor minted before the daemon's first write of the day), and core's `TelemetryLogService.read` resolves the same ambiguity the same way; any component with consumed bytes or a newer retained segment still gets 410.

## Verification

`make verify` (bun run check && bun run test && bun run build) — green.

@@ -1,6 +1,8 @@

-// the v1 stream envelope (reason enums, SSE frame shaping). Refuses replay,
-// cursors, filters, and follow (#81/#82) and never mutates any store.
+// telemetry — the web app's observability feature: the readiness probe, the
+// v1 stream envelope (reason enums, SSE frame shaping), and the stream/
+// sub-feature owning snapshots, filters, cursors, and replay to the
+// caught-up boundary. Refuses live follow (#82) and never mutates any store.
 export * from "./readiness.service";
+export * from "./stream";
 export * from "./stream-envelope.interface";
 export * from "./stream-envelope.render";

diff --git a/apps/web/src/telemetry/stream-envelope.interface.ts b/apps/web/src/telemetry/stream-envelope.interface.ts
index 01b7902..2a9f10d 100644
--- a/apps/web/src/telemetry/stream-envelope.interface.ts
+++ b/apps/web/src/telemetry/stream-envelope.interface.ts
@@ -5,15 +5,41 @@
  * stream-envelope.render.ts.
  */
 
-/** SSE event name of the handshake's single frame. */
+/** SSE event name of the handshake frame, always the stream's first. */
 export const HELLO_EVENT = "score.stream.hello";
+/** Subscribe-time fleet membership and per-project health. */
+export const FLEET_SNAPSHOT_EVENT = "score.snapshot.fleet";
+/** Subscribe-time single-project observation: config, status, health reasons, watermark. */
+export const PROJECT_SNAPSHOT_EVENT = "score.snapshot.project";
+/** One correlated dated-log line. */
+export const LOG_RECORD_EVENT = "score.log.record";
+/** Replay boundary: every durable record up to the captured mark was sent. */
+export const CAUGHT_UP_EVENT = "score.stream.caught_up";
+/** Carries a WarningReason envelope; also the follow seam's frame (#82). */
+export const WARNING_EVENT = "score.stream.warning";
+
+/** SSE event per stored telemetry signal. */
+export const TELEMETRY_RECORD_EVENTS = {
+  event: "score.telemetry.event",
+  span: "score.telemetry.span",
+  metric: "score.telemetry.metric",
+} as const;
 
 /**
  * The whole safe-error vocabulary: a reason from this union is everything an
  * error response says. Paths, environment values, stack traces, and raw
  * command output are never present.
  */
-export type WarningReason = "CONFIG_UNPARSEABLE" | "SEGMENT_UNREADABLE";
+export type WarningReason =
+  | "CONFIG_UNPARSEABLE"
+  | "SEGMENT_UNREADABLE"
+  | "SUPERVISOR_UNREADABLE"
+  | "FILTER_UNKNOWN"
+  | "FILTER_INVALID"
+  | "CURSOR_UNPARSEABLE"
+  | "CURSOR_EXPIRED"
+  | "RECORD_UNPARSEABLE"
+  | "FOLLOW_NOT_IMPLEMENTED";
 
 export interface ApiWarning {
   readonly reason: WarningReason;

diff --git a/apps/web/src/telemetry/stream/cursor.render.test.ts b/apps/web/src/telemetry/stream/cursor.render.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a5adc86
--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/web/src/telemetry/stream/cursor.render.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+import { expect, test } from "vitest";
+import { decodeCursor, encodeCursor } from "./cursor.render";
+
+const components = [
+  { project: "score", source: "telemetry" as const, segment: "2026-08-15", byte_offset: 120 },
+  { project: "score", source: "log" as const, segment: "2026-08-15", byte_offset: 0 },
+  { project: "other", source: "telemetry" as const, segment: "2026-08-14", byte_offset: 7 },
+];
+
+test("composite cursor round-trips every component", () => {
+  expect(decodeCursor(encodeCursor(components))).toEqual(components);
+});
+
+test("garbage and mis-shaped cursors decode to undefined, never throw", () => {
+  for (const value of [
+    "",
+    "not base64!!",
+    Buffer.from("[1,2]").toString("base64url"),
+    Buffer.from('{"project":"score"}').toString("base64url"),
+    Buffer.from(
+      '[{"project":"score","source":"db","segment":"2026-08-15","byte_offset":0}]',
+    ).toString("base64url"),
+    Buffer.from(
+      '[{"project":"score","source":"telemetry","segment":"today","byte_offset":0}]',
+    ).toString("base64url"),
+    Buffer.from(
+      '[{"project":"score","source":"telemetry","segment":"2026-08-15","byte_offset":-1}]',
+    ).toString("base64url"),
+    Buffer.from(
+      '[{"project":"score","source":"telemetry","segment":"2026-08-15","byte_offset":1.5}]',
+    ).toString("base64url"),
+  ]) {
+    expect(decodeCursor(value)).toBeUndefined();
+  }
+});
